chart.label: Round-trip time over time for every endpoint of {{name}}
chart.note: One line per endpoint, each point the slowest round trip in a {{seconds}} s slot — so a spike is never smoothed away, and the line sits above the average beside it. The scale is logarithmic, so 4 ms and 400 ms are both readable; nothing is clipped. A dashed line is the route to an endpoint that answers nothing: the round-trip time to a router on the way there, not to the endpoint itself. A break in a line is probes that did not come back.
chart.failed: The chart could not be drawn ({{reason}}). Every figure it would show is in the list below.

picker.heading: Running applications
picker.hint: Pick up to {{limit}}. Choosing one monitors the whole application — every process it is running under, and anything it launches. Nothing is read from inside them — only which addresses they talk to.
picker.unavailable: The application list could not be requested
picker.unsupportedPlatform: This build cannot list applications on this operating system
picker.refused: The system refused to list running processes
picker.more: Showing {{shown}} of {{total}} applications — narrow the search to see the rest

badge.egressConflict: Probe may not follow this app's route

passive.heading: This endpoint's own traffic
passive.note: Measured from the traffic itself, without sending anything. Not a round-trip time: nothing here times a request against its answer. How evenly the data arrives is what a player feels as stutter, and it includes whatever cadence the server chose — which is why it is shown beside the route rather than instead of it.
passive.updatesUnknown: Not enough arrivals yet to time them

path.heading: Path to this endpoint
path.note: This endpoint answers nothing we can send, so these figures belong to the deepest router that does answer on the way there. It is not the round-trip time to the server: how much further the server sits is unknown.
path.hopUnknown: No hop on the route is answering

quality.uncorroborated: Only the last hop is off — may be that router, not the path

position.reached: The endpoint answered the trace itself
position.nothingAnswered: No router on the way answered; expiry messages are probably filtered locally
position.insideThisNetwork: The route stops inside your own network
position.insideTheAccessNetwork: The route stops inside your provider's network
position.beforeAnyLongHaulLink: The route stops on public infrastructure, before any long-distance link
position.beyondALongHaulLink: The route stops past a long-distance link

egress.via: This app's traffic leaves from {{address}}, and the probe follows it
egress.viaNamed: This app's traffic leaves via {{interface}} ({{address}}), and the probe follows it
egress.probe: The probe cannot follow it and leaves from {{address}} instead
egress.probeNamed: The probe cannot follow it and leaves via {{interface}} ({{address}}) instead
egress.unknown: Egress address unknown; probes follow whatever route the system picks

flow.notPermitted: This account may not open a tracing session, so UDP endpoints and traffic counters are missing — TCP endpoints are still found. Adding your account to the local “Performance Log Users” group once, from an elevated prompt, restores them. The app never does this for you.
flow.stopped: The tracing session stopped — something else on this machine took it over. UDP endpoints and traffic counters are missing until it is back; the app is retrying every second.
flow.unavailable: Per-process flow events are unavailable on this system, so UDP endpoints and traffic counters are missing. TCP endpoints are still found.

settings.languageHint: More languages are added as data; no part of the app has to change.
settings.countryHint: Chooses the domestic baseline list. Nothing is detected from the network — this app never asks anyone where you are.
settings.intervalHint: How often each baseline target is probed. Longer intervals leave more of the probe budget for the applications you monitor.
settings.autostartHint: Off unless you turn it on. Reflects what the system reports, not what was requested.
settings.privacyNote: All measurements stay on this machine. The app sends nothing anywhere except the probes on these lists.

problem.unreadable: The settings file could not be read; defaults are in use.
problem.malformed: The settings file could not be understood; defaults are in use and your file was left untouched.
problem.notWritable: Settings cannot be saved on this machine; changes last until you quit.
